Hi Sylvia — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short proposal that outlines three candidate SKU mixes (memory-first, latency-first, and cost-hedged). I'll summarize the high-level tradeoffs below so procurement has something to read quickly.

Summary (high level)
- H100 (memory + fp8 throughput): best for long-context gen-chat and heavy kv-cache retention; higher $/hr but reduces OOM risk and avoids frequent model sharding for 40k token contexts. Good for your internal evals and p99 latency targets when pinned.
- A100 (balanced): solid middle ground for throughput and memory; lower unit cost vs H100 for many gen workloads but can require more aggressive tiling for 40k contexts. Better if you want stable reserved capacity with predictable throughput.
- L4 (cost/latency optimized for smaller models): very cost-efficient for the 2B embedder and some rerank slices; not suitable as main gen-chat host for long contexts. Great as burst/hedge fleet for demo spikes.

Recommended paths we propose (two options)
1) 12‑month Reserved Primary + Lease Burst: Commit to a mixed reserve pool (majority A100, subset H100 for long-context model instances) + L4 pool for burst demos. Automatic routing rules move short-requests to L4, long-context to H100.
2) Short Reserve Window + Rolling Lease: Smaller reserve (A100) for steady baseline; lease additional H100 capacity nightly or on-demand during extended eval windows. This reduces commitment but increases $/token during heavy evals.

Key decision points for your team
- Do you want to treat long-context gen-chat as a critical SLA-backed service (favor H100 reserve)?
- Is the CFO comfortable with a primarily reserved commitment or would a lease-heavy hedge be preferred?

Next steps: I'll loop in Karthik and Ben for a technical runbook and ops hedging playbook. If procurement confirms target budget range, we can produce a side-by-side cost projection (reserved vs lease) by EOD Monday.

Grace / team / Sylvia,

Thanks for the context and the capacity snapshot — I ran a quick simulation with three workload slices and included an attachment (sku_latency_memory_tradeoff.xlsx) with our assumptions. High level recommendation follows.

Recommendation (ops-forward)
- Baseline commit: 8 x A100 (40GB) nodes for steady-state throughput. Rationale: A100 gives predictable throughput for gen-chat at a lower committed cost than H100; easier to autoscale within reserved pool.
- Memory anchor: 2 x H100 nodes reserved and pinned for long-context gen-chat variants that require 40k token KV retention. Rationale: H100 avoids frequent tiling and p99 regressions for very long contexts. Keep these pinned to model-version labels for safety.
- Hedge / burst: 10 x L4 instances on lease (or spot-enabled L4 pool) to handle demo spikes and offload short-chat and embedder requests. L4s will be auto-routed for requests under 2k tokens and non-critical rerank/embedding workloads.

Operational playbook highlights
- Prefix caching: keep a shared KV cache for gen-chat warmups on H100 nodes during scheduled eval windows to avoid cold-start OOMs.
- Eviction policy: if only H100 capacity remains constrained, use automatic degradation to A100 for truncated context with a graceful fallback message (we also recommend a quantization-simulated test to confirm quality).
- Autoscale knobs: burst to leased L4 within 60s for sudden demo spikes; scale H100 up only during planned eval windows.

Cost sketch (monthly, ballpark)
- Reserved: 8 x A100 + 2 x H100 = predictable baseline (approx. $XXXk/month reserved).
- Lease: L4 pool variable — expect $YYk additional in months with >2 demo spikes. Exact numbers in attached sheet.

Open questions for Sylvia / procurement
- Commitment horizon (12 vs 24 months)? 24 months reduces reserved unit price materially but increases lock-in.
- Are you comfortable with a small H100 reserve as the memory anchor versus using aggressive sharding on A100?
